items.prompt: You ___ wear a uniform here; we have a casual dress code.

explanation.en: No obligation is don't have to; mustn't would mean it is forbidden.
explanation.es: Mustn't es «prohibido»; «no hace falta» es don't have to.

optionNotes.en: Mustn't means forbidden, which does not fit a casual dress code.
Must would mean it is compulsory.

items.prompt: Cyclists ___ ride on the pavement in the town centre. It is against the law.

optionNotes.en: This would mean it is not necessary.
Needn't means it is not necessary.

items.prompt: Sorry, I can't stay. I ___ be at the airport by nine to meet my sister.

explanation.en: Have to expresses an obligation caused by circumstances.

optionNotes.en: This would mean it is not necessary, which contradicts can't stay.
Mustn't means forbidden, which does not fit.

items.prompt: Last year all first-year students ___ attend an induction week.

explanation.en: Must has no past form, so use had to.
explanation.es: Must no tiene pasado: had to.

optionNotes.en: Must cannot refer to the past.
Correct: had to for a past obligation.
Have to is present; last year needs the past.

items.prompt: If the flight is cancelled, we'll ___ find another way to get there.

explanation.en: Must has no form after will; use will have to.
explanation.es: «Tendremos que» es we'll have to, no we'll must.

optionNotes.en: Had is past and cannot follow will.
